title: Claudia Sheinbaum Confirms Her Attendance at the APEC Summit in November
author: Alonso Urrutia and Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Alonso Urrutia and Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alonso%20Urrutia%20y%20Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz)
originally appeared in the [September 24, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/24/politica/la-presidenta-
confirma-su-asistencia-a-la-cumbre-de-la-apec-en-noviembre), Mexico's premier
left wing daily newspaper._

President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo confirmed her attendance at the summit of
the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), which will take place in the
city of **Shenzhen, China, on November 18 and 19**. During her press
conference, she explained that one of the reasons she decided to attend is
that Mexico will organize the next meeting. “There we are going to receive,
let’s say, **the baton to hold APEC in 2028**.”

With Sheinbaum Pardo’s participation, it will be **only the second time that
Mexico attends the summit** since the governments of the Fourth Transformation
came to power in 2018. In November 2023, President Andrés Manuel López Obrador
attended the meeting held in San Francisco. On that occasion, López Obrador
held bilateral meetings with the world’s main leaders.

He met with the President of the People’s Republic of China, Xi Jinping, and
with the then head of the White House, Joe Biden, who was the one who extended
the invitation to attend the summit and to meet, on that occasion,
bilaterally. Likewise, he held a meeting with the then Prime Minister of
Canada, Justin Trudeau.

For this year, according to the program of APEC (an organization of 21
countries, among them China, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Australia,
Mexico, Chile, and Peru), the topics to be addressed, announced at the time by
the Chinese government under the slogan _Building an Asia-Pacific Community to
Prosper Together_ , are expected to include an analysis of **protectionist
trends in the world and the anti-globalization stances** that have permeated
some countries.
